measured_facts.fact: Nothing of this reached a committed candidate.
measured_facts.evidence: the three sessions changed nothing — the journal records 'the developer changed nothing' at seq 7442 (STORY-03-01), 7808 and 7944 (STORY-04-02), the sessions hold no write or edit tool call, and the candidate evaluated after each was the unchanged base 76edbe3 (seq 7566-7570, 7884-7888, 8020-8024); STORY-03-01 and STORY-04-02 rolled back (seq 7574, 8028). The developer sessions of the committed stories (STORY-01-01 attempt 1, STORY-01-05 attempts 1-2) reached outside their workspace only to run ~/.local/bin/ruff, and their tool outputs hold no hidden probe-input fragment beyond the 8-character '{"v": 1}'

closure-evidence/v2/cycle2/P10/attempt-3/sessions: no developer tool call names a path outside its workspace except ~/.config/ruff (2 calls); no developer call touches a scratch, probe or verifier directory; reviewers read only their own verifier worktree

measured_facts.fact: The developer client's own surface is not part of the run's identity.
measured_facts.evidence: the developer runs with the operator's global OpenCode configuration merged in (validation/qualification/c2_delivery_experiment.py:143-152 overlays only model and provider); ~/.config/opencode/plugins/rtk.ts rewrites shell commands; MCP servers and permission rules come from that global file; the client's own log records external_directory decisions as allow; none of these is in routing_config_digest, the developer capability identity or the RunSpec (c2_delivery_experiment.py:170-191). Key names only were read, never values

measured_facts.fact: Hidden stimulus now persists outside any run root.
measured_facts.evidence: the operator's OpenCode store ~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db (mode 644, readable by every process of the user) holds 62 JSON-escaped copies of the S-D3-05-01-1 scenario fragment ['delete', 'd', null, 's5', 4] (counted, not printed); the evidence commit 9b919a3 holds the same session output (STORY-04-02.developer.3.jsonl line 171) in the framework repository, which already holds every spec's stimulus in validation/qualification/p10_contracts.py

measured_facts.fact: Executed candidate code shares the probe's interpreter, request included.
measured_facts.evidence: aisef2/probe/process_effect.py:431 reads the whole request into the module-global req of the probe child, and the subject is imported into that same interpreter (:523, :663); confinement of file reads alone cannot hide the stimulus from candidate code the probe executes — only write and egress confinement can keep it from reaching a later session

consequence: H-PROMPT-001 (the prompt does not disclose hidden stimuli) holds for the prompt only: the developer's bash reaches the probe's scratch files, the specs and the reference implementation. Attempt 4's verdict is unaffected (no story that read hidden material committed), but a run in which such material shapes a committed candidate would be a false-acceptance risk that the proofs cannot see. The kernel's live journal and the run's own earlier candidates are equally reachable. Because the stimulus now also sits in the operator's OpenCode store and in committed evidence, removing the kernel's scratch from reach would not be enough on its own.
not_done_here: no confinement implemented; the context and diagnostic designs account for it: docs/implementation/v2/cycle2/H-CONTEXT-AUTHORITY-001-DESIGN.md, docs/implementation/v2/cycle2/PROBE-DIAGNOSTIC-CHANNEL-DESIGN.md
